note: Eight guards, chosen by how many applied Tier A findings cite each as proof; none had ever been falsified. Batch 1's four transferable lessons were applied as an explicit checklist per guard (probe-flag semantics, degenerate fixtures, sibling-app boots are not automatically miscitations, throw-based harnesses stopping early is normal). This auditor started the Vite dev server (npm run dev, :3400) — nothing was listening at start.

guards.citationAnalysis: Both questions the task posed, answered separately. DOES IT WORK: yes — healthy, breaks (A) and (B) confirm it. IS IT CITED IN THE RIGHT PLACE: no for gmt-renderer.md, yes for render-and-shaders-core.md (which scopes engine/RenderPipeline.ts, engine/BloomPass.ts, engine/ShaderBuilder.ts, engine/UniformSchema.ts — the harness imports the first directly). guards.falseNegativeAnalysis: The filter cannot weaken the check. It matches on the LINE leading characters, and real code never begins a line with * or //; a trailing comment on a code line leaves the start untouched so that line is still scanned. Deliberately not implemented as comment-stripping, which would have been unsafe — naive // stripping eats real code after a string containing https://.

findings.summary: engine-gmt's bucket/accumulation path has no runtime guard of any kind. Gutting GmtBucketHost.resetAccumulation() — the per-bucket `this.engine?.pipeline.resetAccumulation()` call — leaves test:bucket-convergence green, typecheck green, and (by the rule's own analysis) smoke:tsaa green since fluid-toy never imports RenderPipeline.
findings.rationale: Found while answering the citation half of the test:bucket-convergence falsification. The doc side is now fixed (commit 6046dcc2 states the gap plainly instead of claiming coverage), so no finding rests on a false premise — this is about whether the gap should be closed. THE CATCH: the natural fix is to extend test-bucket-convergence.mts to drive GmtBucketHost, but that host wants a live FractalEngine with a worker and a GL context, which is exactly why the existing harness mocks at the RenderPipeline seam instead. Options: (1) leave it, and rely on the rule text now saying 'unguarded, verify by hand' — cheapest, and honest; (2) add a node-level harness that constructs GmtBucketHost against a stub `engine` object with only `pipeline` on it, asserting the per-bucket transition calls through — narrow, cheap, and would have caught break (D), but it tests one delegation rather than the bucket path; (3) extend smoke:engine-gmt to drive a short bucket render in-browser and assert on accumulation counts — real coverage, materially more work, and bucket renders are slow. RECOMMENDATION: (2) as a floor, since the delegation is precisely the thing that broke silently, then (3) only if bucket-seam regressions recur. Not applied: it is new coverage rather than a repair, which the protocol puts in the owner's hands.

findings.summary: The only thing keeping the shared modulation dispatcher honest about slider-space compose is a TEXT match on the applier source. Block [6] proves composeModulatedValue itself composes correctly, but calls it directly — so no assertion anywhere observes that applyTarget actually routes through it. The regex is now broader (commit e2ba7eeb) but it is still a text match, and a third spelling would evade it again.
findings.rationale: Found by falsifying block [9]. The applied fix closes the specific hole that was proven, so nothing rests on a false premise — this is about whether the check should be behavioural instead of textual. THE CATCH: making it behavioural means driving applyTarget with a CURVED target and asserting the result matches composeModulatedValue rather than plain addition, which needs a fixture with a curved routing — and per this batch own findings a fixture whose curve is effectively linear would make the new assertion vacuous, so it has to be chosen deliberately (the cube/log params in block [1] are the obvious candidates). Options: (1) leave the broadened regex — cheapest, and it now catches both natural spellings; (2) add a behavioural assertion alongside it that runs applyTarget against a curved target and compares to composeModulatedValue, keeping the regex as a cheap belt-and-braces; (3) replace the regex with the behavioural check — cleaner to read, but loses the ability to flag a raw add on a path the fixture does not happen to exercise. RECOMMENDATION: (2). Not applied: it is new coverage requiring a fixture design choice, not a repair of something proven broken.

summary.headline: Three of eight could not fail on something they claim to cover, and a fourth was cited on a rule whose files it cannot reach. Worst: smoke:engine-demo printed "modulation tick runs" in its success banner while the render loop was completely dead (counter 0 -> 0) — it was a console.warn and the smoke collects console.error only. Second: check:zindex allowlisted the two files that DEFINE the z-index scale, so a hardcoded zIndex: 9999 on Layer.tsx portal div — collapsing the entire tier table — passed check:zindex, test:zindex and typecheck together.

perGuardVerdict.test:bucket-convergence: wrong-target (harness healthy; citation removed from gmt-renderer.md)
perGuardVerdict.test:session-hold: healthy — strongest of the batch, 4 breaks / 4 mechanisms all red
perGuardVerdict.smoke:camera: healthy — carries its own anti-vacuity guard, which reproduces

batch1LessonsApplied.probe-flag semantics: Applied to smoke:engine-demo. The failure channel question was decisive twice: a dead render loop reports as console.warn and TickRegistry own 3s no-ticks safety net is ALSO a console.warn, while the smoke collects console.error only — so two independent safety nets both missed it.
batch1LessonsApplied.degenerate fixtures: Caught a live instance and prevented shipping another. smoke:engine-demo step 5 probe accepted "Randomize" OR "Demo" anywhere in body text and read true with the entire HudHost returning null; simply adding a throw would have shipped a tautology, so the probe was tightened to the pill own key label FIRST, then asserted. Also checked test:session-hold (non-degenerate: audio.isEnabled defaults false and the fixture seeds true) and test:param-mapping.
batch1LessonsApplied.sibling-app boots are not automatically: smoke:camera and smoke:help-menu both boot fluid-toy.html and both are legitimate — proven by breaks in engine/plugins/Camera.ts, engine/plugins/camera/presetField.ts and engine/plugins/Help.tsx all going red, rather than assumed from the URL.
batch1LessonsApplied.throw-based harnesses stopping early: Observed in smoke:camera, smoke:help-menu and smoke:engine-demo; recorded as normal, not reported as a defect.
